pull.title: KAFKA-20400: Enable VersionedKeyValueStoreWithHeaders in DSL
pull.body:
Ref https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/KAFKA-20400

This PR extends the KIP-1285 headers-aware state store infrastructure to versioned key-value stores. Prior to this change, KIP-1285 was implemented for timestamped, windowed, and session stores, but versioned stores silently dropped record headers on both the write and read paths.

Reviewers: Alieh Saeedi <asaeedi@confluent.io>
---

Record headers carry metadata (tracing IDs, schema references, auth tokens) that downstream processors and interactive query clients may need. Versioned stores (RocksDBVersionedStore) were the only remaining store type that discarded headers. This PR closes that gap.

---
 API changes:

VersionedRecord<V> -- Added Headers headers field with new constructors and a headers() accessor. Existing constructors default to empty headers (backward compatible).

Stores.persistentVersionedKeyValueStoreWithHeaders(String, Duration) -- Factory method returning a dual-interface supplier.

Stores.versionedKeyValueStoreBuilderWithHeaders(VersionedBytesStoreSupplier, Serde, Serde) -- Builder factory method.

RocksDBVersionedStoreWithHeaders -- Extends RocksDBVersionedStore, encodes headers into value bytes using [headersSize(varint)][headersBytes][rawValue] format before delegating to the parent store. Decodes on read.

ChangeLoggingVersionedKeyValueBytesStore -- Added put(key, value, timestamp, headers) override to forward real headers to the changelog instead of empty headers.

KeyValueStoreWrapper -- get() now returns VersionedRecord.headers() instead of empty headers; put() forwards headers to VersionedKeyValueStoreWithHeaders when available.

reviews.body: LGTM, thank you for addressing the comments.

review_comments.body: Shouldn't the equals() method also check headers equality?
Also the toString() can include headers?
Aren't headers required here in this default?
is this cast necessary ? Can it be done similar to headerStore and avoid casting on every put

The existing put(key, value, timestamp) unconditionally passes new RecordHeaders(). The headers parameter of the new VersionedKeyValueStoreWithHeaders.put() interface doesn't document whether null is acceptable and the VersionedRecord constructor rejects null headers with Objects.requireNonNull. I think this inconsistency could lead to NullPointer ?

Thanks for review. 

This was an intentional design choice to preserve backward compatibility. VersionedRecord.equals() is a pre-existing contract -- adding headers to it would change comparison semantics for existing code that relies on the current behavior. Headers are metadata, not part of the record version identity (two records with the same value/timestamp but different tracing headers are the same logical version). That said, I can see the argument for consistency with ValueTimestampHeaders.equals(). If the consensus is to include headers in equality, I can make that change -- though it would need a note in the doc about the behavioral change. What do you think?

The default is intentionally headers-discarding for backward compatibility. Existing VersionedBytesStore implementations (like RocksDBVersionedStore) don't know about headers. The default method ensures they continue to compile and work without modification. Only RocksDBVersionedStoreWithHeaders overrides this to actually persist the headers. This follows the same approach used in other interfaces where a new method needs a backward-compatible default.

Good point, fixed. Added a versionedStoreWithHeaders field that is set once during init when the versioned store implements VersionedKeyValueStoreWithHeaders. The put() method now uses this cached reference instead of instanceof + cast on every call.

Good catch. Fixed in two places: (1) ChangeLoggingVersionedKeyValueBytesStore.put(key, value, timestamp, headers) now normalizes null to empty headers before passing to the inner store, preventing NPE in RocksDBVersionedStoreWithHeaders. (2) VersionedKeyValueStoreWithHeaders.put() javadoc now documents `@throws` NullPointerException if headers is null to make the contract explicit.

IMO `headers` should be part of equals and hashCode for consistency.
For backwards compatibility, new RecordHeaders()  will be empty I guess, so behaviour of equals method and hashcode is still ok.

You are right. For consistency with ValueTimestampHeaders.equals() and the general Java convention that all significant fields participate in equality, I will include headers in both equals() and hashCode(). The backward compatibility risk is low since existing code constructs VersionedRecord with the no-headers constructors (which default to empty RecordHeaders), and non-headers stores also return records with empty headers. I will update this in the next push.

> For consistency with ValueTimestampHeaders.equals() and the general Java convention that all significant fields participate in equality

Does it really written by you?

This forwards headers correctly, but nothing upstream supplies them: KTableSource (line 171) and the KTable/KStream aggregate/reduce/filter/join processors all call store.put(k,v,ts,new RecordHeaders()), and this PR doesn't change them. So a KTable materialized with the headers store still persists empty headers end to end. KTableSource (and the aggregation paths meant to carry headers) need to pass record.headers().

This pipes records with headers and the docstring claims header preservation, but it only asserts key/value — never reads back the stored headers. It stays green even though headers are dropped before the store. Read store.get(...).headers() and assert the piped values.
shouldForwardHeadersToChangelog reads the changelog record but asserts only its key, not its headers — so it can't catch headers being dropped. Assert the changelog record's headers here.

This only checks the supplier implements both interfaces; it never calls KeyValueStoreMaterializer.builder() to confirm a versioned+headers supplier routes to versionedKeyValueStoreBuilderWithHeaders (and not the plain versioned builder). The new routing branch — the actual production change here — is untested.
